description: Hi! We’re Eshun Burge and Colton McGill, competing as team Aquanauts in the Tampa, FL Space Apps Challenge. We’re tackling the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge to create a fun, engaging, and interactive learning experience for aspiring space explorers. Excited to build something out of this world!
summary:
Space exploration fascinates children, yet the science behind it is often presented in ways that are either oversimplified or too complex for younger audiences. To bridge this gap, we developed Aquanauts, an interactive astronaut training game that introduces children ages 7–12 to the challenges of living and working beyond Earth.

Players explore a three-dimensional lunar base alongside eight sea-creature astronauts, completing missions focused on the essential systems needed to sustain life on the Moon. Through equipment repairs, resource management, and problem-solving challenges, children learn how life support, energy production, agriculture, and engineering work together to keep a lunar base operational. Each mission builds on previous lessons, culminating in a final challenge that combines the skills players have developed. Quizzes, certifications, and rewards reinforce their progress, while a custom-built physical game board extends the experience beyond the screen.

Drawing on NASA research and real scientific data, Aquanauts transforms complex space science into an accessible, hands-on learning experience. Our goal is to help children understand not only how space exploration works, but also the scientific reasoning and teamwork that make it possible, inspiring greater confidence and curiosity in STEM.
details:
Aquanauts is an interactive astronaut training experience designed to teach children what it takes to establish, operate, and maintain a lunar base. By combining three-dimensional exploration, mission-based challenges, and a physical game board, we created a learning experience in which children can apply scientific concepts rather than simply memorize them.

How Aquanauts Works

Players navigate a three-dimensional lunar base using keyboard or touchscreen controls. Across eight missions, they work alongside a crew of sea-creature astronauts, each specializing in a different system essential to the base's operation. Every mission begins with a short introduction to a scientific concept before challenging players to apply their knowledge through an interactive task.

For example, players might discover that the base's air filtration system has malfunctioned. They must locate the appropriate tools, navigate to the damaged equipment, and complete repairs to restore the system. Other missions introduce energy production, food cultivation, radiation protection, infrastructure maintenance, sustainability, and mission planning. Together, these challenges teach children how a lunar base functions and why its systems depend on one another.

Each mission builds on the skills developed in previous levels. By the final challenge, players must draw on multiple concepts to address problems across the base, reinforcing the importance of planning, resource management, and coordination.

To make these activities accessible to younger players, crew members provide captioned instructions, while a glowing navigation trail guides children toward their objectives. Each mission concludes with a knowledge check that reinforces the lesson and allows players to earn a certification.

Beyond the simulation, Aquanauts includes a connected mission control website where children can track their progress, explore a map of the lunar base, and earn coins and prizes as they complete challenges. Players can also adopt collectible 3D crew pets using their earned coins, creating an additional incentive to continue learning. A dedicated teacher mode allows educators to access individual missions directly, making the experience suitable for classroom demonstrations, guided activities, and independent exploration.

Physical Game Board

To extend Aquanauts beyond the digital environment, we designed and built a physical game board that brings an additional hands-on component to the experience.

The board features a spinning octopus head at its center, five illuminated LEDs, and three rotating dials. These physical elements encourage children to engage with the game's theme through movement, touch, and visual feedback. The dials introduce the idea of adjusting equipment, while the lights reflect the visual language of monitoring systems found in a mission control environment. The spinning octopus head serves as a playful centerpiece that connects the board to Aquanauts' sea-creature characters.

By incorporating physical components, we wanted to make the experience more tangible for children who learn best through hands-on activities. The board complements the virtual lunar base by giving players another way to explore the ideas of operating equipment and managing a space mission.

Educational Benefits and Intended Impact

Our primary educational goal is to help children understand the scientific and engineering challenges involved in sustaining human life on the Moon. Rather than focusing only on individual space facts, Aquanauts introduces the lunar base as an interconnected environment where every system contributes to the safety and success of its crew.

Throughout the eight missions, players explore the relationships between life support, electricity, agriculture, habitat protection, engineering, and limited resources. For example, producing oxygen requires functioning equipment and a reliable energy supply, while growing food depends on access to water, lighting, and a controlled environment. Understanding these relationships helps children recognize why even a small equipment failure can affect the operations of an entire lunar base.

Aquanauts also introduces the importance of making decisions under real-world constraints. Space missions cannot rely on unlimited electricity, water, or replacement equipment. Our lessons encourage players to consider how resources are used, why maintenance matters, and how thoughtful planning can prevent larger problems. These concepts demonstrate that successful space exploration requires more than scientific knowledge alone; it depends on the ability to apply that knowledge effectively.

We also designed Aquanauts to encourage independent learning and experimentation. Players can repeat missions without penalties, allowing them to revisit unfamiliar concepts and learn from mistakes. By avoiding strict time limits and punishment-based mechanics, we create an environment where children can focus on understanding the material rather than rushing to complete tasks.

Beyond scientific knowledge, the experience introduces children to the range of careers and responsibilities involved in space exploration. Operating a lunar base requires engineers, scientists, technicians, mission planners, and many other specialists working toward a common goal. By showing how these disciplines contribute to one functioning environment, Aquanauts encourages children to see STEM as a collaborative field with many opportunities to explore.

Ultimately, we hope children finish the experience with a stronger understanding of what makes life beyond Earth possible and greater confidence in their own ability to approach complex scientific problems.

Development Tools and Technology

We developed Aquanauts using a combination of web development technologies, three-dimensional modeling tools, and game development software.

The website was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Three.js and Vite were used in the browser-based development of the 3D simulation, with Unity also contributing to our team's three-dimensional development process. To construct the lunar environment, we combined freely available 3D models with original assets created using Blender. This approach allowed us to build a detailed environment while dedicating more time to developing the game's educational content and functionality.

Firebase Authentication and Firestore support optional user accounts and progress tracking. We used GitHub to manage our code and publish the application through GitHub Pages, allowing players to access the game directly through a web browser. The application is also integrated with our WordPress website.

During development, we used Claude, an AI assistant developed by Anthropic, to assist with coding, debugging, and testing. We designed our original sea-creature characters using Procreate and created presentation materials using Canva. We also used AI-generated images to visualize potential merchandise concepts, which are clearly identified as AI-generated.

By combining these tools, we developed a digital learning platform that incorporates game development, original artwork, interactive web design, and physical prototyping.

Creativity and Design Considerations

One of Aquanauts' defining features is its combination of an engaging fictional world with realistic scientific challenges. Instead of traditional human astronauts, we created a crew of sea creatures, each with a distinct personality and responsibility aboard the lunar base. Their designs make the unfamiliar environment more approachable for younger children while helping players associate different characters with the scientific systems they operate.

We also wanted the game to feel like an actual lunar mission rather than a collection of unrelated educational activities. Each challenge is connected to a responsibility astronauts would face when maintaining a base beyond Earth. NASA resources, including DONKI space weather observations and OSDR astronaut health research, helped inform our mission scenarios. We also drew on planetary exploration research to introduce realistic environmental conditions and operational challenges.

These scientific references shaped how we approached the game's lessons. Instead of asking children to memorize isolated facts, we wanted them to understand how scientific information informs decisions. For example, learning about solar radiation becomes more meaningful when players must consider how to protect a lunar habitat and its crew.

Another important consideration was accessibility. Because Aquanauts operates through a web browser, players can access the experience without downloading specialized software. Guest access allows children to begin playing without creating an account, while captioned instructions help make lessons understandable in classrooms and other environments where audio may not be practical. Adjustable text sizes, reduced-motion settings, and simplified gameplay options were included to accommodate different learning needs.

We also considered how to keep children engaged beyond individual missions. Features such as progress tracking, daily streaks, collectible pets, certifications, and unlockable rewards provide achievable goals while encouraging players to revisit lessons. The physical game board extends our approach to hands-on learning by introducing a tangible companion to the digital environment.

Throughout development, our team worked to balance scientific accuracy, educational value, and age-appropriate gameplay. We wanted children to enjoy exploring the lunar base while gaining a meaningful understanding of the systems that make space exploration possible.

Aquanauts demonstrates that children can engage with complex STEM concepts when they are given opportunities to explore, experiment, and solve problems themselves. By transforming the responsibilities of operating a lunar base into an accessible learning experience, we hope to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.
